questionText:
Choose the most appropriate option to fill the blank in the given sentence.

Most young poets \\textbf{________} the works of the Great Romantics for guidance.
solution:
Look up to means to respect, admire, or revere someone as a role model.

Look in on means to visit briefly; look out for means to watch out or take care of; look away from means to avert one's gaze.

Vocab Meanings: • Look up to: To admire and respect (आदर करना / आदर्श मानना)
• Look in on: To visit briefly to check on (हालचाल पूछने जाना)
• Look out for: To watch out for; to take care of (ध्यान रखना / सावधान रहना)
• Look away from: To turn one's eyes away from (नज़रें फेर लेना)
conceptTested: Appropriate usage of phrasal verbs based on contextual meaning.

subject: English
questionText: Which of the following options most accurately expresses the meaning of the idiom "to cook the books"?

options.A: To meticulously analyse extensive literature and academic publications to extract relevant data for a thesis.
options.B: To draft innovative, highly creative recipes for a commercial restaurant chain to maximise culinary efficiency.
options.C: To systematically preserve ancient, deteriorating manuscripts through advanced chemical restoration techniques.
options.D: To intentionally falsify corporate accounting records or balance sheets to deceive auditors and investors.
options.a: To meticulously analyse extensive literature and academic publications to extract relevant data for a thesis.
options.b: To draft innovative, highly creative recipes for a commercial restaurant chain to maximise culinary efficiency.
options.c: To systematically preserve ancient, deteriorating manuscripts through advanced chemical restoration techniques.
options.d: To intentionally falsify corporate accounting records or balance sheets to deceive auditors and investors.

solution:
To cook the books is an idiom that means to manipulate, alter, or falsify accounting records and financial data fraudulently.

Options (a), (b), and (c) are literal or irrelevant distractors.

Vocab Meanings: • To cook the books: To falsify accounts or records (हिसाब-किताब में हेराफेरी करना / खातों में गड़बड़ी करना)
conceptTested: Understanding the figurative meaning of common English idioms.

questionText:
The sentence given below is divided into four segments labelled P, Q, R, and S. Read the sentence carefully to determine which segment contains a grammatical, syntactic, or idiomatic error. Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: Every sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any).
(P) Although the newly appointed directors were initially eager to exculpate the CEO by any wrongdoing, / (Q) they found themselves entirely at odds with the legal counsel's aggressive strategy, / (R) which sought to attribute the catastrophic financial losses directly to systemic institutional negligence / (S) rather than to external, unpredictable market forces.
solution:
Segment (P) contains a prepositional error. The verb exculpate takes the preposition from (or of), not by ("to exculpate the CEO from any wrongdoing").

Segments (Q), (R), and (S) are grammatically and syntactically correct.
conceptTested: Correct prepositions following specific verbs (exculpate from).

subject: English
questionText:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

Please help the injured man at once.

options.A: The injured man is requested to be helped at once.
options.B: The injured man should be helped at once.
options.C: Let the injury man be helped at once.
options.D: You are requested to help the injured man at once.
options.a: The injured man is requested to be helped at once.
options.b: The injured man should be helped at once.
options.c: Let the injury man be helped at once.
options.d: You are requested to help the injured man at once.

solution:
An imperative sentence expressing a request starting with "Please" changes into passive voice using "You are requested to + V1...".

Thus, the correct passive transformation is "You are requested to help the injured man at once."
conceptTested: Conversion of imperative sentences expressing a request into passive voice.

questionText:

Select the letter corresponding to that specific segment as your answer. (Note: Every sentence contains exactly one error. Ignore errors of punctuation, if any.)

(P) Equipped with advanced bio-luminescent sensors, / (Q) the deep-sea submersible sounded cautious as it navigated / (R) the uncharted hydrothermal vents, monitoring for volatile acoustic signatures / (S) that could signal an imminent volcanic eruption.
solution:
Segment (Q) contains an error of adverb vs. adjective usage or semantic appropriateness. The submersible's navigation or sonic probing is described; if using "sounded" to mean taking depth/navigational soundings, an adverb modifying the action of sounding (cautiously) is required.

Segments (P), (R), and (S) are grammatically correct.
conceptTested: Correct use of adverbs to modify verbs and actions instead of adjectives.

subject: English
questionText:
In contemporary cognitive science, human judgment is increasingly understood as a product of layered neural and psychological mechanisms rather than a purely rational calculus. Decisions that appear deliberate are often (A) by unconscious biases that subtly recalibrate perception before conscious deliberation even begins. This recognition has significantly undermined earlier models of rational agency, suggesting instead that cognition is dynamically constructed in real time.

Fill in the blank (A) with the correct word.
solution:
Mediated means brought about, influenced, or conveyed as an intermediary mechanism, which perfectly describes decisions shaped by unconscious biases.

Aggravated means made worse; intensified means made more intense; obstructed means blocked.
conceptTested: Contextual vocabulary and logical word choice in advanced descriptive passages

subject: English
questionText:
Within this framework, behavioural economists argue that heuristics, while computationally efficient, can (B) systematic errors in probabilistic reasoning, particularly under conditions of uncertainty and informational overload. Such errors are not incidental but structurally embedded within the architecture of human cognition.

Fill in the blank (B) with the correct word.
solution:
Engender means to cause, give rise to, or produce. Heuristics give rise to systematic errors in reasoning.

Obviate means to avoid or prevent; mitigate means to make less severe; circumscribe means to restrict or limit.
conceptTested: Contextual vocabulary and logical word choice in advanced descriptive passages

subject: English
questionText:
Clinical psychology has similarly evolved, with therapeutic paradigms increasingly encouraging individuals to (C) entrenched cognitive schemas rather than merely suppressing symptomatic expressions of distress. This shift reflects an understanding that maladaptive thought patterns are self-reinforcing and resistant to superficial correction.

Fill in the blank (C) with the correct word.
solution:
Deconstruct means to analyze or dismantle a complex structure into its basic components to understand or modify it, contrasting with merely suppressing symptoms.

Entrench and perpetuate mean to establish firmly or prolong; acquiesce means to accept reluctantly without protest.
conceptTested: Contextual vocabulary and logical word choice in advanced descriptive passages

subject: English
questionText:
Nevertheless, scholars caution that public discourse often (E) complex psychological constructs into overly simplistic explanatory frames, thereby obscuring the nuanced interplay between cognition, emotion, and environment.

Fill in the blank (E) with the correct word.
solution:
In this context, flatten (used figuratively or loosely in non - standard/informal subject discourse to mean oversimplify or reduce multi - dimensional nuance into a single simplistic dimension) corresponds to reducing complex constructs into overly simplistic explanatory frames.

Magnify, diversify, and authenticate contradict the idea of creating overly simplistic frames.
conceptTested: Contextual vocabulary and logical word choice in advanced descriptive passages
